text:
marta: fyi CI job eval/metrics-sanity failed on the new gptq-quant model run, looks like a metric mismatch :thinking:

 eval-bot: Job eval/metrics-sanity #482 failed (timeout: 45m). Logs: https://ci.internal/jobs/482

 devon: saw the logs. BERTScore compute crashed with "TypeError: expected float, got '0.912'" from metrics/bertscore.py:45

 sam: ah that smells like JSON serialization -> stringified floats when we cache intermediate scores. We hit that before with rouge dumps.

 nina: repro snippet from logs:
```
# metrics runner
preds = load_json('preds.json')  # some values are strings
score = bertscore(preds['scores'])
```

 ravi: on the implementation side, two things to verify:
- tokenization mismatch (do we use sacrebleu tokenizer for BLEU vs sacremoses?)
- numeric types: numpy floats -> tolist() vs json dumping

 marta: also related: pass@k harness test failing in CI because candidate dedup changed candidate count. The formula we implement assumes n_total includes deduped unique samples.

 luis: we should standardize pass@k contract. Recommend this implementation note in runner:
```
# pass@k for sampled unique outputs
# given n unique samples and c correct candidates
pass_at_k = 1 - comb(n-c, k) / comb(n, k)
```
(assumes combinatorics on unique candidates)

 devon: +1. Also note edgecase when k >= n: pass@k = 1 if any correct present.

 sam: for BLEU we added smoothing method=2 by default. Is that what everyone expects? It changes small-sentence behavior.

 nina: project-wide expectation is BLEU corpus-level w/ smoothing for short refs. But we need to document which tokenizer & corpus-level vs sentence-level we use.

 ravi: BERTScore gotcha: IDF weighting depends on ref corpus tokenization. If we compute idf on tokenized refs in-PR vs in-prod we'll diverge. Use fixed idf table per dataset version.

 marta: CI fix plan:
1) Add schema validation step to preds.json to ensure numeric fields are not strings.
2) Update bertscore impl to coerce numeric strings with float(x) and log warnings.
3) Add unit tests: small_json_with_string_floats.json -> runner should normalize.
4) Add pass@k contract test for dedup cases.

 luis: can we add a quick smoke test in the docker image to run metrics on a tiny fixture so we catch serialization issues early? eval-image:test-smoke

 devon: yep will open a PR. Will reference internal ticket INFR-1292 and include a short failing example.

 sam: regression note on ROUGE-L: our current implementation picks sentence-level LCS, causing lower corpus recall. We should switch to concatenated-document LCS for leaderboard consistency.

 nina: +1 on concatenated LCS for system-level evaluation. But keep sentence-level as an option for per-example diagnostics.

 ravi: also saw occasional flaky BERTScore approx equality due to GPU nondeterminism in faiss embedding lookup. Add seeding and tolerance in tests: assert_almost_equal(score, expected, places=3)

 marta: one more subtlety: calibration measurement in evals/metrics.py uses equal-width buckets (10). For skewed confidences (0.99 majority) equal-frequency bins are more stable. Propose switching to quantile bins for reliability diagrams.

 luis: can you add a tiny plot helper in metrics.visualize.reliability that outputs CSV so dashboards can ingest? Avoid dependencies on matplotlib in CI.

 devon: putting together PR: https://git.redwood/infr/metrics-fixes/pulls/57

 eval-bot: Linked PR #57 triggered CI workflow eval/metrics-sanity -> queued

 sam: post-PR we should run a canary on the dedicated cluster with a small sample to validate numeric parity vs older results and record diffs in the dashboard.

 marta: thanks everyone. I'll add follow-up tasks in the eval backlog and pair with devon on the schema validator tomorrow. :thumbsup:
